newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Police arrest 120 outside European leaders hotels.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest 120 outside European leaders hotels.

text.p: Dutch police on Monday night arrested about 120 protesters who were shouting outside hotels where leaders attending a European Union summit were staying.
"We arrested them around midnight under a local law for disturbing the public order," Amsterdam police spokesman Klaas Wilting told Reuters on Tuesday.
He said they would be released from custody on Tuesday afternoon after paying fines.
But he said another 340 people arrested on Sunday night after they assembled for a demonstration outside Amsterdam's police headquarters remained in custody.
Wilting said the public prosecutor's office would determine what charges they would face.

About 150 people went on the rampage in central Amsterdam on Saturday afternoon, smashing windows and overturning a police vehicle, after a big street march against the economic hardship caused by the path towards European economic and monetary union.
Security around the summit venue is tight, with police in large numbers patrolling the streets and riot police on standby in case of trouble.
